app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

symptoms.potential_symptom: DNS resolution failures when charging cards causing checkout/payment errors
symptoms.evidence: Multiple frontend-proxy error traces (e.g. traceID fd760c2748d10ded450fd547b11f38ee, 7b746bd41bab1531225abe6710c41ebd, 1025f623c8c00c48d5d0fcab15cffd92) show identical error: "13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving". Payment pod is present (payment-6c5f448889-rnhrq Running). Symptoms indicate the payment service's outbound DNS lookups are failing, preventing card charges.

symptoms.potential_symptom: Connections to frontend are intermittently refused (clients see ECONNREFUSED)
symptoms.evidence: Many error traces show callers (frontend-proxy/frontend-web) failing to connect to frontend with: "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.181.21:8080" (examples: traceIDs 9eadcf4cde9f255a0b5dc9cc622b810c, 1a840b088a2514e5717e6a00cbfed72c, afedc18dedc356134586bec2cf3eddfc). Frontend pod frontend-559ccb996b-vffdl is Running and Ready (pod IP 10.244.1.26), suggesting refused connections target the service ClusterIP (10.96.181.21) and indicate networking/service endpoint or port-level refusal rather than pod crash.

final_report.root_cause:
There are two independent failure modes that together caused the observed checkout and connectivity errors: 

1) Payment checkout failures: The payment service repeatedly failed to charge cards because it could not resolve the external payment gateway host (traces contain: "dns: A record lookup error: lookup badAddress on 10.96.0.10:53: server misbehaving"). Current cluster state shows the payment pod is Running/Ready and CoreDNS pods and Service are healthy, so the immediate cause is intermittent DNS resolution failures on the outbound path from the payment service (most likely upstream DNS or transient CoreDNS forwarding errors), which made the payment service unable to reach the external payment processor. 

2) Intermittent ECONNREFUSED to frontend: Callers (observed as frontend-proxy / frontend-web in traces) were connecting to the wrong/stale ClusterIP 10.96.181.21:8080. That IP is owned by the cart Service (clusterIP=10.96.181.21), not the frontend Service (clusterIP=10.96.32.121). Clients using the stale/wrong ClusterIP were therefore routed to the wrong service and saw connection refusals. Separately, the frontend pod itself is missing a PAYMENT_ADDR environment variable, so it was not even configured to call the payment Service directly — a configuration gap that would prevent successful payment integration even when service endpoints are healthy.
